title: Triangular coordinates make a restricted series distinguished
statement:
Let $F$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. For $r\geq1$ let $D_r=F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ be the ring of series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}c_
u x^
u$ such that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many $|c_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition, Cauchy multiplication and Gauss norm $\|f\|=\sup_
u|c_
u|$; put $D_0=F$. For each nonzero $f\in D_r$ there are positive integers $N_1,\ldots,N_{r-1}$, an isometric $F$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $D_r$ with $\sigma(x_i)=x_i+x_r^{N_i}$ for $i<r$ and $\sigma(x_r)=x_r$, and a unit $v\in D_{r-1}$ such that, writing $v\sigma(f)=\sum_{j\geq0}a_jx_r^j$ with $a_j\in D_{r-1}$, there is an integer $d\geq0$ for which $a_d=1$, $\|a_j\|\leq1$ for $j<d$, and $\sup_{j>d}\|a_j\|<1$. For $r=1$ the list of integers is empty and $\sigma$ is the identity.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] for the complete Gauss-norm rings $D_s$, their ultrametric and product inequalities, and their isometric last-variable regrouping. Scalar multiplication satisfies $\|cf\|=|c|\|f\|$ directly from the coefficient supremum. Choose a nonzero coefficient $u$ of $f$. The nonempty finite set of coefficients with $|c_\nu|\ge|u|$ contains one of greatest absolute value, say $\lambda$; every coefficient outside it is smaller than $|u|$, so $|\lambda|=\|f\|>0$. Set $g=\lambda^{-1}f$. Its norm is one. Let $p$ be the finite polynomial consisting of exactly the coefficients of $g$ of absolute value one, and put $h=g-p$. There is a common bound $\|h\|\le\rho<1$: take $\rho$ to be the maximum of $1/2$ and the finitely many absolute values strictly between $1/2$ and one. Thus $p\ne0$, every nonzero coefficient of $p$ has absolute value one, and $\|p\|=1$.

proof.text: If $p$ is nonconstant, apply [lem-trf-polynomial-shear-leading-coefficient] over the commutative ring $F$ with $n=r$. Obtain positive $N_i$, $d>0$ and a nonzero coefficient $c$ of $p$ such that its substituted polynomial has the form $c x_r^d+\sum_{j<d}b_jx_r^j$. In particular $|c|=1$. If $p$ is constant, set $c=p$, $d=0$ and choose all $N_i=1$; its substitution is just $c$. These cases give the same scalar-leading-term formula with $d\ge0$. For $r=1$ the lists are empty and both polynomial substitutions are the identity.

proof.text: In the complete normed $F$-algebra $D_r$ of [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], the tuples $x_i+x_r^{N_i}$ and $x_i-x_r^{N_i}$ for $i<r$, with last entry $x_r$, have norms at most one. All other target-algebra hypotheses of [lem-per-tate-banach-substitution] hold: the scalar norm identity is coefficientwise, and completeness, nondegeneracy, $\|1\|=1$, ultrametricity and submultiplicativity are supplied by the Gauss-norm node. Apply substitution to get contractive continuous $F$-algebra maps $\sigma,\tau$. Each composite fixes every variable by the explicit calculation $(x_i+x_r^{N_i})-x_r^{N_i}=x_i$ and fixes constants. Uniqueness in the substitution node, applied to the tuple $(x_i)$, makes both composites the identity. Hence $\|\sigma(z)\|\le\|z\|=\|\tau\sigma(z)\|\le\|\sigma(z)\|$, proving that $\sigma$ is an isometric automorphism. On polynomials it is exactly the substitution of Step 2 by finite addition and multiplication. For $r=1$, uniqueness gives $\sigma=\operatorname{id}$.

proof.text: Regroup $\sigma(g)=\sum_{j\ge0}A_jx_r^j$ using [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion]. Contractivity gives $\|\sigma(h)\|\le\rho$ and $\|\sigma(p)\|\le1$. Its polynomial part has degree $d$ in $x_r$ and scalar leading coefficient $c$, so $A_d=c+e$ for some $e\in D_{r-1}$ with $\|e\|\le\rho$, and every row with $j>d$ has norm at most $\rho$. Every row, including $j<d$, has norm at most one since $\|\sigma(g)\|=1$. These row bounds follow from the isometric regrouping: each row norm is bounded by the norm of the whole series. The strict uniform tail estimate is therefore $\sup_{j>d}\|A_j\|\le\rho<1$, rather than merely a separate strict inequality at each index.

source.place: Definition 1.1.2 and Exercise 1.1.3(1), PDF p.3; Exercise 1.2.8(3), PDF p.7; Theorem 1.1.5 introductory paragraph, PDF p.4. Agent reconstruction of the coordinate argument, not a proof printed in Conrad.

proof.text: Work in the complete ring $D_{r-1}$ from [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], which includes $D_0=F$. Put $q=-c^{-1}e$, so $\|q\|\le\rho<1$ and $A_d=c(1-q)$. The finite sums $s_m=\sum_{k=0}^m q^k$ are Cauchy: for $n>m$ the ultrametric and product bounds give $\|s_n-s_m\|\le\rho^{m+1}\to0$. Let $s$ be their limit. Each $\|s_m\|\le1$, hence $\|s\|\le1$. The finite identity $(1-q)s_m=s_m(1-q)=1-q^{m+1}$ passes to the limit, since multiplication by a fixed element is continuous by the product bound; thus $s$ is a two-sided inverse of $1-q$. Consequently $w=c^{-1}s$ is a two-sided inverse of $A_d$ with $\|w\|\le1$. In fact $\|A_d\|=1$: otherwise $1=\|c\|\le\max(\|A_d\|,\|e\|)<1$. Also $1=\|A_dw\|\le\|A_d\|\|w\|$ gives $\|w\|=1$. This writes out the inverse and its estimate using only completeness and finite geometric sums.

source.place: Definition 1.1.2 and Exercise 1.1.3(1), PDF p.3; Exercise 1.2.8(3), PDF p.7; Theorem 1.1.5 introductory paragraph, PDF p.4. Agent reconstruction of the coordinate argument, not a proof printed in Conrad.

proof.text: Set $v=\lambda^{-1}w\in D_{r-1}$, a unit with inverse $\lambda A_d$. Since $f=\lambda g$ and $\sigma$ fixes $F$, we have $v\sigma(f)=w\sigma(g)$. Under the ring regrouping of [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], its rows are $a_j=wA_j$. Therefore $a_d=1$, $\|a_j\|\le\|w\|\|A_j\|\le1$ for $j<d$, and $\sup_{j>d}\|a_j\|\le\rho<1$. Multiplication by the fixed $w$ also preserves decay of the row norms. All required data have now been constructed. When $d=0$ the lower-row condition is empty; the inverse argument still applies. When $r=1$ we used no coordinate change, and $v\in D_0=F$ as required.
